_comment: Single source of truth for both implementations. Neither the C++ nor the Python pipeline may hard-code any value that appears here; tests/test_config_is_sole_source.py enforces it.

camera._comment: Fixed eye-to-hand RGB-D camera above the table, looking down. The four intrinsics below describe the reference 640x480 stream; docs/ALGORITHM.md S1 gives the rule that carries them to another sensor mode.
camera.intrinsics_note: Square pixels, so fx == fy, and the principal point is the image centre: (640-1)/2 = 319.5, (480-1)/2 = 239.5. A different sensor mode is the same optics reading a different window of the same array, so the focal length in pixels tracks the vertical resolution only (fx = fy = fy_ref * H / reference_height) and the principal point is recentred on the new image. Scaling all four by W / reference_width instead would claim a wider mode stretches the image, and would put cy at 317.34 on the 480-row 848x480 stream, which no sensor reports. The rule is the identity at the reference resolution, which is why these four values are what they are.
camera.T_base_cam_note: Camera optical frame (x right, y down, z forward) looking straight down from 0.85 m, 0.30 m in front of the robot base: cam +z maps to base -z, cam +x to base -y, cam +y to base -x. det(R) = +1.

workspace._comment: Axis-aligned crop in the panda_link0 frame. Anything outside is not reachable and not worth clustering.

plane._comment: RANSAC table removal. Sample indices come from a precomputed uniform table (see ransac_table) so the two implementations cannot diverge through their PRNGs.
plane.min_horizontal_cos_note: cos(15 deg); a candidate whose normal tilts further than this from +z is not a table and scores zero.
plane.clearance_note: Points within inlier_threshold + clearance of the refit plane, and everything below it, are removed.

grasp.grasp_depth_note: How far below the cluster's highest point the TCP is placed.

ik._comment: Damped least squares with a null-space pull toward q_neutral. Seeded from q_neutral every frame, not from the previous solution, so per-frame cost does not depend on tracking history.
ik.nullspace_note: Measured, not guessed. At this damping, with the gain at 0.1, the solver converged on 0 of 100 real grasp targets: I - J^T (J J^T + lambda^2 I)^-1 J differs from a true null-space projector by O(lambda^2) while lambda > 0, so the bias leaks into task space and the solve stalls at a fixed point 2.87 mm from the target against a 0.5 mm tolerance. The failure is in position, not orientation; the orientation error stays inside 1.45 mrad of a 5 mrad tolerance. An earlier version of this note put it at 198 mrad, from a sweep taken before the S5 wrist fold existed, and that figure does not reproduce. With a genuine pseudo-inverse projector it converges but costs an SVD per iteration. Seeded from q_neutral every frame the solution already sits near the neutral posture, so the bias buys nothing here and the term is off. docs/METHOD.md section 11 has the damping against gain grid.

sensor._comment: Depth-sensor error model. Read by harness/make_dataset.py only -- neither pipeline sees it -- but it lives here so a corpus is reproducible from one file, and because RANSAC's difficulty is set by these numbers.
sensor.axial_noise_note: sigma(z) = coeff * z^2 metres, the usual structured-light axial model. 1.08 mm at the 0.85 m table, against a 6 mm inlier threshold.
sensor.dropout_note: Dropout probability ramps linearly from baseline_dropout_prob to grazing_dropout_prob as |cos(incidence)| falls from grazing_cos_threshold to 0. Steeply viewed surfaces -- object side walls -- mostly return nothing, as on a real sensor.

scene._comment: Synthetic table scene sampled by harness/make_dataset.py. Not read by either pipeline.

table.tilt_note: A few degrees of tilt, so plane refit and the plane-height lookup in S5 are exercised rather than trivially satisfied by z = 0.

objects.min_gap_note: Clear separation between footprints, so 6-connected 1 cm voxels never merge two objects into one cluster.
objects.primary_area_ratio_note: The largest footprint must beat the runner-up by this factor, so the cluster S4 selects is unambiguously the object the manifest calls truth.
objects.place_note: Placement stays inside the camera footprint at every supported resolution and 0.30-0.58 m from the base, where a top-down Panda grasp is comfortably reachable.

shading._comment: RGB is rendered only because a real node has to decode it; the pipeline never reads colour.

ros._comment: Topic and frame names shared by the bag writer and the ROS 2 nodes.

ransac_table.count_note: iterations * 3 float64 values in [0,1), little-endian. Generated by tools/make_ransac_table.py.

implementation._comment: Blocking parameters. These change how the work is issued, never what it computes: any value gives bit-identical output, only the memory traffic differs. Chosen by measurement on the machine in docs/TOOLCHAIN.md. This held only after the int16 inlier accumulator in the Python plane stage was widened to int32; before that, a block above 32767 points wrapped and changed which plane RANSAC chose.
implementation.ransac_block_note: Points scored against all candidate planes at a time. 512 x 128 float64 is 512 KiB, which keeps the distance block inside L2.

analysis._comment: Read by harness/analyze.py and harness/compare_outputs.py only. Here rather than in the harness so a published percentile can be traced to the definition that produced it.
analysis.percentile_method_note: Nearest observed sample, never interpolated between two. A latency that was never measured is not a latency, and at n = 2000 the p99.9 sits between the second and third slowest samples where interpolation would invent a value.
analysis.equivalence_tolerance_note: Absolute, in metres, radians or dimensionless matrix entries, matching docs/ALGORITHM.md. Far tighter than any physical effect and far looser than the 1e-15 noise from differing summation orders.
analysis.tail_percentile_note: The percentile the garbage-collection attribution is run against: frames at or above it are the tail whose cause is in question.

rate_sweep._comment: harness/rate_sweep.py drives each implementation at these fixed control rates over the frame store, with absolute deadlines taken from a monotonic start.
rate_sweep.datasets_note: Two resolutions, because the rate at which an implementation starts missing deadlines is a property of the pair and not of the language.
